# spec.builders.hrf { #fmrimod.spec.builders.hrf }

```python
hrf(
    *variables,
    basis='spm',
    hrf_fun=None,
    nbasis=None,
    span=None,
    contrasts=(),
    modulators=(),
    center_modulators=True,
    pool_modulators=False,
    durations=None,
    lag=0.0,
    subset=None,
    prefix=None,
    id=None,
    norm=None,
    normalize=False,
    summate=True,
)
```

Build an `HrfTerm`.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name              | Type                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Default   |
|-------------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| *variables        | str                  | Events-table column(s) whose levels (or values) become regressors, e.g. ``"trial_type"``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `()`      |
| basis             | HRF \| str           | HRF name (``"spm"``, ``"spmg2"``, ``"spmg3"``, ``"fir"``, ``"bspline"``, ``"tent"``, ``"fourier"``, ...) or an `HRF`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `'spm'`   |
| nbasis            | Optional\[int\]      | Number of basis functions for flexible bases (FIR bins, spline knots, ...).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `None`    |
| span              | Optional\[float\]    | Flexible bases only: the window in seconds the ``nbasis`` functions cover (default 24 s). For an FIR with one bin per scan, as Nilearn's ``fir_delays=range(n)``, pass ``nbasis=n, span=n * tr``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `None`    |
| modulators        | Sequence\[str\]      | Names of parametric-modulator columns in the events DataFrame. Each modulator expands into one additional regressor: the unmodulated boxcar scaled by the modulator's per-event value. Listing order is irrelevant — fmrimod does not orthogonalize modulators against each other.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `()`      |
| pool_modulators   | bool                 | If True, each modulator is one regressor across all levels of the term (centered over all its events), contrasted as ``"rt"``; if False (default), one slope per level (``"trial_type:rt.face"``). Pooling is the model Nilearn builds from a ``modulation`` column.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `False`   |
| center_modulators | bool                 | Mean-center each modulator at the input-variable level (on the raw per-event scalar that becomes the boxcar amplitude), before convolution. Default ``True``, matching `EventVariable`'s ``center=True`` default and the post-Mumford modern-correct workflow. Set to ``False`` for exact R ``fmridesign`` parity or when the modulator's absolute scale carries the analytic meaning. See the *parametric modulators* tutorial for the full discussion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `True`    |
| norm              | Optional\[NormMode\] | HRF normalization mode. Leave as ``None`` for the raw canonical scale.  - ``"spm"`` — divide by the *sum* of the HRF evaluated on   Nilearn's reference grid (``time_length=32``,   ``oversampling=50``). Matches Nilearn's ``hrf_model="spm"``   scale. - ``"unit_peak"`` — divide by the absolute peak of the HRF on   its span. Mirrors R's ``normalise_hrf``. - ``"unit_integral"`` — divide by the trapezoidal integral so   the continuous integral equals 1. - ``"unit_peak_per_basis"`` — multi-basis only: each column is   divided by *its own* absolute peak so every column has unit   peak. Use when the basis columns are heterogeneously scaled   (e.g. an ``as_hrf`` wrapper around a hand-built basis).  **Multi-basis behaviour (SPMG2 / SPMG3 / FIR / B-spline).** ``"spm"``, ``"unit_peak"``, and ``"unit_integral"`` all derive a *single* scalar from the canonical column (column 0) on the reference grid and apply that same scalar uniformly to every basis column. This preserves the physical interpretation of the derivative / dispersion columns as latency / shape *perturbations* of a fixed-amplitude canonical — ``β_derivative`` units stay commensurate with ``β_canonical`` units. ``"unit_peak_per_basis"`` rescales each column independently, which breaks that interpretation but is useful when the columns are not basis functions in the SPM sense (e.g. an arbitrary multi-channel kernel). For ``basis="spmg2"`` / ``"spmg3"``, prefer ``"spm"`` (Nilearn-compatible) or ``"unit_peak"`` (R-aligned) over ``"unit_peak_per_basis"``. | `None`    |

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

Informed basis sets (``basis="spmg2"`` / ``"spmg3"``) follow R
fmrihrf: the second column is the analytic time derivative
``dh/dt`` and the third (SPMG3) is SPM's dispersion difference.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> hrf("trial_type")
>>> hrf("trial_type", basis="spmg3")
>>> hrf("trial_type", basis="fir", nbasis=8)
>>> hrf("trial_type", basis="fir", nbasis=8, span=16.0)  # 8 x 2 s bins
>>> hrf("trial_type", norm="spm")  # Nilearn-compatible scale
>>> hrf("trial_type", "block", subset={"task": "memory"})
>>> hrf("trial_type", modulators=("rt", "accuracy"))  # auto-centered
>>> hrf("trial_type", modulators=("rt",), center_modulators=False)
>>> hrf("trial_type", modulators=("rt",), pool_modulators=True)  # one rt column
```
